mainEntity.name: Why does HSA3 work without mineral wool?

acceptedAnswer.text: The micro-perforated top layer and the chambers behind it form many small resonators (Helmholtz principle). Air friction in the fine holes turns sound energy into heat. A deliberate difference in phase and sound pressure between front and rear chamber – an impedance jump – creates the absorption. The multi-layer core distributes the rest before it reaches the carrier plate. There are no fibres that soak up moisture or shed.

mainEntity.name: Why is HSA3 better than conventional insulation at low frequencies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porous absorbers need a lot of thickness and mass for low frequencies – and hardly reach structure-borne noise radiated by housings. HSA3 works through its geometry: locally resonant structures specifically damp the range where compressors, fans and pumps drone. The result: slimmer, lighter enclosures with less pressure drop and therefore more unit capacity.

mainEntity.name: Is HSA3 suitable for BESS and outdoor use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. HSA3 is non-combustible (class A1 to EN 13501-1, the highest classification) – especially important for battery storage. The metal is weather-resistant and designed for permanent outdoor use, where chillers and heat pumps are usually installed.

mainEntity.name: Does it always have to be a full enclosure?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Because HSA3 is modular, individual noise sources can be treated: the compressor, the tonal fan noise (blade passing frequency) or the whine of inverters. The modules sit close to the source, can be removed individually and save space and material compared with full cladding – ideal for retrofits.

mainEntity.name: How is the supporting structure built?

acceptedAnswer.text: From anodised aluminium industrial profiles 45 × 45 mm with T-slot, joined with standard corner brackets and slot nuts – bolted, not welded. Every part is available from stock, so short lead times instead of one-off fabrication, with no paint line and no weld inspection. The design is proven for self-supporting frames over 12 m and originated in 2015 with the Silent-Mode and ForCoTech brands.

Low frequencies find every gap. That is why we seal frames with sealant rather than tape and avoid vibrations. What is laborious in a prototype becomes reproducible in series production – and therefore standard in our custom builds too.

mainEntity.name: How does an HSA3 project run and how is the effect verified?

acceptedAnswer.text: From a single source: acoustic design from first consultation to detail, made-to-fit manufacturing of the HSA3 components, site logistics and installation by regional, quality-assured teams – and finally an on-site (in situ) differential measurement that proves the effect.
